answer: Each identity must anchor one reef of opal shards on a quartz lattice where the k-th reef holds k(k+1)(k+2)/6 opal credits, so fake k pays that many and each new clone costs k(k+1)/2 more than the last. Ten fakes pay 715 credits; a hundred pay 4,421,275. Two reefs sharing one quartz lattice both crack at the close, so lattices can never be pooled across clones.
